change: Rewrote the 26 letter pages to answer 'letter X' searches (10-17); added 'for Kids' to titles (10-18); stroke-order diagrams, writing-first layout and a printable tracing sheet (10-18).
hypothesis: Pages that answer 'letter X' / 'what letter of the alphabet is X' directly, with a clearer kids-focused title, earn a higher CTR at their current ~position 9-10 and gradually better positions. (Reconstructed from the commit messages; written down after the change shipped.)
confounders: Four changes shipped within two days on the same pages, alongside site-wide fact-checks and template-filler removal (34a0329, 10-17); their effects cannot be separated.
next_action: Interim check each week; decide keep/revise after 2026-11-18.

hypothesis: Fuller number lessons gain impressions and position for bare-number and 'number N for kids' queries (currently position ~13-19).
confounders: Same-week site-wide edits. Hero image stopped lazy-loading on these pages too (hero-not-lazy, load-time only).

hypothesis: Shape pages that answer 'how many sides/corners' queries directly gain impressions and position.
confounders: Same-week site-wide edits. Hero image stopped lazy-loading on these pages too (hero-not-lazy, load-time only).

confounders: Same-week site-wide edits. Hero image stopped lazy-loading on these pages too (hero-not-lazy, load-time only).

change: Expanded hub pages that Search Console listed as 'Crawled - currently not indexed' (animals, body parts, electronics) plus the numbers hub.
hypothesis: More substantial, unique hub content gets these hubs indexed and showing impressions within ~4-6 weeks.

next_action: Watch URL-inspection coverage state for these hubs each week.

change: Removed loading="lazy" from the fetchpriority="high" hero image on 316 pages (all lazy heroes except the 26 letter pages, held until their experiment is evaluated).
hypothesis: The hero is requested without waiting for layout, so LCP improves. Any search effect is expected to be small and slow; impressions are tracked only as a guard against regressions.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: LCP from PageSpeed Insights / CrUX on a sample (lion, count-and-match, kiwi) before and after deploy
confounders: Overlaps the running number, shape, kiwi and hub experiments. Performance-only: pages are not held back from other recommendations (holds_back false), so later snippet/content edits on these pages overlap this experiment's search metrics.
next_action: Interim check weekly; evaluate after 2026-11-19. Apply to the letter pages after 2026-11-18.

change: Wrapped the CDN-hosted PNG hero on 36 pages (34 worksheets, downloads, word-matching) in <picture> with the existing same-origin WebP (e.g. count-and-match 529 KB PNG -> 76 KB WebP).
hypothesis: Smaller hero images load faster on mobile, improving LCP; search impact expected to be small.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: Hero transfer bytes and LCP (PSI) on count-and-match and downloads before/after deploy
confounders: Same pages also got hero-not-lazy in the same deploy; the two can't be separated. Performance-only: pages are not held back from other recommendations (holds_back false), so later snippet/content edits on these pages overlap this experiment's search metrics.

change: Added a 'Keep Learning' block of 3-6 links to related lessons, games and worksheets before the footer on 9 root game pages that were dead ends (only a JS Back button and footer links). scripts/add_game_next_steps.py. Batch 2 (same day, before </body>): mirror-words-learning, phonic-numbers, phonic-rhyming, phonic-segmenting, tracing-letters-and-numbers, which had no header, footer or links at all.
hypothesis: Visitors who finish a game get a next step, so more organic sessions view a second page; crawlers get a path from these pages into the /learn/ lessons. Search clicks on the 9 pages themselves are not expected to change.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: GA4, organic sessions landing on the 9 pages: views per session and share of sessions with 2+ page views, 28 days before vs after, compared with organic sessions landing on the other root game pages (control: shapes, fruits, vegetables, numbers, birds, vehicles, planets, plants, phonics, match-animals, match-shapes, odd-even, colours-sorting and the other root games without the block). Watch Bing clicks on colors/bodyparts/organs for regressions.
confounders: Adds internal links to hubs in 2026-10-18-unindexed-hubs (learn/animals, learn/numbers, learn/body-parts, learn/phonics), which can speed their crawling and blur that experiment. Low traffic: about 100 organic sessions/28 days on these pages, so only a large change is detectable. Batch 2 pages were part of the control until moved into the treatment on 2026-10-23; batch 2 deployed the same day as batch 1. Baseline (GA4, 2026-09-25..10-22): 76 organic sessions landed on the treatment pages with 2.93 views/session; many visitors already went on via the Back button to the homepage and /games.html, so the pages were not complete dead ends.

ga4_engagement.note: Control = organic sessions landing on any other page (treatment pages are matched first; '(not set)' is excluded). The 32 untreated root game pages had only 26 organic sessions in the 28 days before, too few to compare.

change: vercel.json: images (png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif/svg/ico/avif) served with Cache-Control 'public, max-age=604800, stale-while-revalidate=86400' instead of Vercel's default max-age=0, must-revalidate.
hypothesis: Repeat page views and return visits stop revalidating every image, so they load faster and use less bandwidth. Search metrics are not expected to move.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: Live response headers on sample images; Vercel bandwidth and CrUX/PSI field LCP over 28 days. Trade-off: an image replaced under the same file name can take up to a week to update for returning visitors.
confounders: Site-wide, so there is no control group; deployed during hero-not-lazy and hero-webp-worksheets (PSI lab LCP uses a cold cache, so those lab measurements are unaffected). Performance-only: pages are not held back from other recommendations (holds_back false), so later snippet/content edits on these pages overlap this experiment's search metrics.
next_action: Check live headers after deploy; evaluate after 2026-11-20.

hypothesis: Both hubs are 'Discovered - currently not indexed' and were the thinnest hubs on the site. A clearer description of the section may help them get crawled and indexed; their child pages may follow.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: URL Inspection coverage state and last crawl for the two hubs and their 14 child pages, re-checked weekly. Only 2 pages, so this is a case observation, not a statistical test.
confounders: Google may crawl the hubs anyway over time; image-cache-week deployed the same day.
next_action: Request indexing for both hubs; re-inspect weekly; evaluate after 2026-11-20.

Before: only Blog/index.html linked to them.

change: Search snippets rewritten to match what searchers ask: word-matching.html title/description/og (was 'Animals & Birds'-specific); banana.html title/description lead with 'Do bananas grow on trees?'; saturn.html adds a 'What is Saturn made of?' FAQ (page + FAQPage JSON-LD) and mentions it in the description.
hypothesis: Bing (last ~90 days): word-matching.html 495 impressions / 1 click at position ~2 for 'word matching game(s) for kids'; banana.html 354 / 4 ('facts about bananas for kids', 'what type of plant do bananas grow on'); saturn.html 188 / 0 ('what is saturn made of for kids'). A snippet that answers the query should raise click-through at similar positions.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: Bing Webmaster page stats (weekly buckets, see the report's Bing appendix): clicks and impressions per page, 8 weeks before vs after. Most of these pages' search traffic is Bing, which the automated evaluation does not cover yet. Banana and Saturn also need Google to recrawl them first.
confounders: word-matching.html is in hero-webp-worksheets and banana/saturn in hero-not-lazy (performance changes, 2026-10-22). Bing may rewrite titles. Click counts are small, so only a large change is readable. Found after deploy: most of the Bing demand behind word-matching and saturn was an August burst (word-matching: no Bing impressions since 2026-08-28; saturn since 2026-09-18). Banana still has ~15-35 Bing impressions a week. Expect little measurable effect until that demand returns.
next_action: Request indexing for banana and saturn; evaluate after 2026-11-20 on Bing clicks.

change: Question-led titles and answer-first descriptions: airplane.html 'How Do Airplanes Fly? Airplanes for Kids: Lift, Parts & Facts'; apple.html 'Apple Facts for Kids: Health Benefits, Types & How Apples Grow', description leading with fiber, vitamin C and floating (25% air). Title, description, og and twitter tags only.
hypothesis: Flagged by the weekly report's Bing check: over ~13 weeks airplane.html had 622 impressions / 12 clicks at avg position 6.0 (site peers at that position: ~28 clicks expected), apple.html 289 / 3 (~13 expected). The old titles already contained the query words, so this tests whether leading with the question and a direct answer lifts CTR at the same positions. Weaker hypothesis than ctr-batch-1.
primary_measure_outside_gsc: Bing page clicks vs the rest of the site (weekly report, Bing table). Airplane demand is steady (30-96 Bing impressions/week since July); apple fell from 30-55/week in September to 3/week in October.
confounders: Both pages are in hero-not-lazy (performance, 2026-10-22). Low CTR at positions 6-9 may be mostly position and SERP features, not the snippet. Apple's seasonal decline means its result may be unreadable.
next_action: Evaluate after 2026-11-20 on Bing clicks (airplane mainly; apple likely unreadable).
